# Gate 2 — Clean Self-Update

*Child of the v2-floor Execution Program [803a7141](803a7141.md). This is the per-gate dev-spec for Gate 2 of the v2 floor — it runs the dev-pipeline end-to-end and cuts its own release (v1.78.0), per the v2/v3 reframe: no big-bang v2.0.0.*

---

## The outcome this gate buys

An OS that people adopt must be able to update to a new Tropo version **without losing the user's own work.** That is the entire gate. Everything below is in service of one provable property: *when a Studio applies a Tropo update, every OS component moves to the new version and not one user-authored file is touched* — unless the user explicitly approved a migration that touches it.

The update machinery already exists. It was fully designed and built once (the v0.2.x–v0.3.0 era) against Update Spec v1.0 [61e5699d](61e5699d.md) and v1.1 [fd7ec4d4](fd7ec4d4.md), and the apply-update playbook [71f186cf](../playbooks/71f186cf.md) is on disk at v1.1 with migrations, dry-run-diff, defensive-skip, and version-gating all working. The bones are strong. What is missing is two-fold:

1. **The machinery predates One Home.** ADR-045 [ca6e5824](ca6e5824.md) collapsed governed content into a single `vault/` tree and gave Tropo's shipped components the `tropo-` filename prefix. The apply-update playbook still assumes the old world: `.tropo/`-as-kernel, a `system/updates/` subtree (now dissolved — confirmed gone from disk), and a path-by-path SHA-drift heuristic for deciding what to preserve. That heuristic is exactly the thing One Home makes obsolete.
2. **The Update API was never built.** Two accepted-but-unbuilt tasks — the Update API [f1d4b9e6](f1d4b9e6.md) and the apply-time incompatibility halt [b8f2d6a3](b8f2d6a3.md) — are the missing front door. Without them a Studio cannot discover an update or fail safely on a version gap.

This dev-spec reconciles the machinery onto One Home, builds the missing front door, re-homes the state machine, carries the proven v1.1 mechanisms forward verbatim, and lands the floor test that *proves* the property.

---

## The load-bearing idea: replace a heuristic with a predicate

This is the heart of the gate. Read it first.

**Old world (heuristic).** The built playbook decides what to preserve by *inspecting content*. Step 3c (the "seed-propagate / SHA-drift" block, canonical file lines ~413–434) walks `.tropo/seed/vault/*.md`, and for each seed UID that already exists in the active tree it computes a SHA256 of both copies and, on drift, surfaces a "reconcile if needed" bulletin. This is a path-by-path guess: *compare bytes, hope we guessed right about what is user-owned.* It is fragile, and One Home makes it unnecessary.

**New world (predicate).** ADR-045 gives us a deterministic rule keyed on the **filename namespace**, not on content:

| Filename pattern | Meaning | Update behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `tropo-*` (e.g. `tropo-rebuild-vault.py`, `tropo-create-task.md`) | OS component — Tropo's shipped standard library | **REPLACE** on update. This is the OS; updating it is the whole point. |
| `<slug>-<uid>` or bare `<uid>.md` (e.g. `004d0994.md`) | User / studio content | **PRESERVE** — never touched, *except* by a migration the user has explicitly approved via the dry-run-diff gate. |

Because cross-references resolve by UID and the `tropo-` token is a display/filename convention (ADR-045 Decision §3, OP-12 name≠address), this predicate is a **one-line rule, not a content diff.** "User files are sacred" (Update Spec v1.0 §3.3) stops being a hopeful heuristic and becomes a structural guarantee: the apply engine decides replace-vs-preserve by looking at the filename, full stop.

**Concrete reconciliation of the playbook:**
- **Delete** the entire SHA-drift / seed-propagate block (old Step 3c, ~lines 413–434). Seed propagation by content-diff is superseded by the namespace predicate.
- **Add** an explicit Rule in the Rules section stating the predicate above, citing ADR-045 [ca6e5824](ca6e5824.md).
- **Sweep** every `system/updates/...` path (47 occurrences in the canonical file) to the re-homed One-Home location (see §"Re-home the state machine").
- **Sweep** every "`.tropo/` is the kernel; updates freely modify it" assumption (22 occurrences) to the One Home boundary. **Replace/preserve has THREE categories, not two** (Orpheus O25 finding at the One-Home doc-spec close, 2026-06-28): (a) `vault/tropo-*` OS components → **REPLACE**; (b) the `.tropo/` **bootstrap floor** — boot config + the OS P0 primitives (SELF-HEALING / HUMAN-NAVIGATION) + schema + generated catalogs + concierge + orientation — is ALSO shipped OS → **REPLACE** (it is OS, just not under `vault/` and not `tropo-*`-named); (c) `vault/<slug>-<uid>` user content → **PRESERVE**. The earlier "`.tropo/` is only a pointer" framing was inaccurate and is corrected here — the apply engine must treat the `.tropo/` floor as replaceable OS, not skip it.
- Bump the playbook to **v2.0** with a changelog row naming the One Home reconciliation.

> Note: do NOT rewrite the v1.1 migration machinery while reconciling — only its *paths* and the replace-vs-preserve decision change. The dry-run-diff protocol, defensive log-and-skip, idempotency, divergence-halt, and no-auto-rollback are carried forward verbatim (see §"Carry forward verbatim").

---

## The agent face: Po runs the update *(Mike-directed 2026-07-01)*

**The machinery below is never the customer's interface — Po is.** Mike's directive: *"We will use Po as our agent on the inside to facilitate this for our customer studios."* This is not new design; it activates a mode Po already carries by Mike's own pair-design:

- **The role exists, locked.** Po's charter (194c4935) names three modes; mode 3 is the **safe-integration steward** ("when a new Tropo release lands, you help the Studio's own agents integrate the new capabilities safely"). Lane P-operational [9f2f458d] (LOCKED v1.0, Mike-V55 walk 2026-05-29) specs it: *"New Tropo release lands in the Studio → Po boots in release-adoption-helper mode, loads release-delta context, walks the principal through new capabilities."* Po ships with every release; her boot path IS the shipped concierge (`.tropo/concierge/activate.md`).
- **The concierge flow exists, stale.** The shipped concierge already carries the full update UX by design — boot-protocol step 6 (scan pending, describe in plain language, detection ≠ apply), a Section 5 handling flow, an "Apply an update" capability wired to the apply-update playbook, never-without-explicit-approval. But it points at the dissolved `system/updates/pending/` — dead-on-arrival in a customer Studio. The committed-substrate row above reconciles it.
- **The arc, end to end (every customer Studio):** Po discovers (boot-time scan of the re-homed state machine + Update API check, offline=skip) → surfaces after the greeting in plain language → dry-run-diff → **owner approves explicitly** → apply (namespace predicate: `tropo-*` replaced, user files sacred) → record to `vault/updates/` history → walks the owner through what changed. On a version gap, Po delivers the `migration_required` message verbatim — a path, not a wall.
- **In Argo, Po P1 dogfoods it.** Po's first boot is held (Metis-G86 lean, Mike-agreed) until the fresh v1.77 build + a clean front-door re-walk — which lands *before* this gate builds (Track B sequencing). P1's first real work: run the Po walk (acceptance criterion above) against the Gate-2 build. Our agent on the inside, tested on the inside first.

*(Federation note, named not built: the update check is the first live upstream surface of Po's federation-ambassador mode — Studio ↔ Tropo releases. Deeper federation is v3+.)*

---

## Scope — what this cycle builds

### 1. Reconcile apply-update [71f186cf] onto the One Home boundary  *(REFACTORED)*

As above. The acceptance bar: the canonical file `vault/playbooks/71f186cf.md` contains zero `system/updates/` paths, no `.tropo/`-as-kernel assumption, no SHA-drift block, and a new explicit namespace-predicate Rule citing ADR-045. Playbook version → v2.0.

### 2. Build the Update API [f1d4b9e6]  *(NEW)*

Endpoint: `GET .../updates/check?version=<current_version>` (target host per the task: `api.tropo-ai.com/updates/check`).

Three response shapes (per the task body):
- **Up to date** — `{ "current": "...", "updates": [] }`
- **Update(s) available** — `{ "current", "minimum_supported", "updates": [ { version, type, description, url, min_compatible } ] }`
- **Migration required** — `{ "migration_required": true, "message": "<plain-language instructions>" }`

Hard requirements (from the task):
- **LLM-callable** via curl or equivalent; **no auth required to check.**
- **Graceful on malformed/unknown version strings** — never a 500 or a stack trace; return a well-formed response the agent can reason about.
- **Offline behavior = skip.** If the network is unreachable the user-agent simply skips the call; there is no error state. The update path must degrade to "no update info available, proceed normally."
- **Stable package URLs** — packages are served at non-expiring URLs (not signed URLs that expire).

### 3. Build the apply-time incompatibility halt [b8f2d6a3]  *(NEW)*

Option A (selected with Mike, G35 — Option B automated-migration is deferred to Teams/Enterprise). The contract:
- A **pre-flight check** at the very start of apply-update (before any operation executes): if the manifest carries `migration_required: true`, deliver the manifest's `message` field **verbatim** and **halt cleanly.**
- **No silent failure. No dead end.** The user always has a next step — the message itself is the next step.
- The halt message is the manifest's `message`, not a generic error string.
- This composes with the existing `min_compatible` version-gate check already in the playbook (Step 2): the API-driven `migration_required` halt is the *front-door* version gate (caught at check-time), and the playbook's `min_compatible` halt is the *apply-time* backstop. Both must produce plain-language version-gap guidance.

### 4. Re-home the update folder state machine  *(NEW / REFACTORED)*

`system/updates/` was dissolved by One Home and is gone from disk. The pending/applied/failed state machine + the update-history index must move into a One-Home location under `vault/`. Proposed home: **`vault/updates/`** with `pending/`, `applied/`, `failed/`, and a One-Home update-history index. (Talos confirms the exact path against the live One-Home folder conventions at build time and against any folder CAPSULE; the requirement is *one home under `vault/`*, governed, not the old `system/` subtree.) Every read/write in the playbook and the thin `.tropo/` pointer must target this location.

### 5. Carry forward verbatim the v1.1 mechanisms  *(preserve, do not redesign)*

These are built, proven, and explicitly NOT to be redesigned. They carry into v2.0 unchanged in behavior (only their paths move):
- **Dry-run-diff + approve-on-diff** — the concierge runs each migration in dry-run, presents the aggregate file-level diff, and captures explicit user approval *before* any write (Spec v1.1 §14.3.1, §6.3 Step 3).
- **Commit-divergence-halt** — if the commit-phase diff diverges from the approved dry-run diff, halt; the user approved the dry-run, not the new state.
- **Defensive log-and-skip** — unexpected file structure inside a migration scope is a skip with a recorded reason, NOT a failure; a non-zero skip count with `result: PASS` is valid.
- **Idempotent migrations** — running a migration twice produces the same state as once.
- **Plain-language version-gap guidance** — on a version gap, name the specific intermediate versions in order; a path, not a wall (Spec v1.1 §6.4 refinement; playbook Step 2).
- **No auto-rollback** — partial states are left honest and inspectable; the engine does not attempt automated reversal (Spec v1.0 §6.4; Spec v1.1 §14.5).

### 6. Re-validate the two reference migrations + the vault-steward  *(REFACTORED)*

Against the single `vault/` tree + the namespace rule:
- `.tropo/playbooks/migrations/migrate-file-status.playbook.md` — scopes resolve under `vault/`; the migration never writes a `tropo-*` OS component or anything in `.tropo/`; idempotent; defensive log-and-skip intact.
- `.tropo/playbooks/migrations/migrate-index-format.playbook.md` — index scope resolves to the One-Home index; never rewrites user `<slug>-<uid>` content as content; idempotent; defensive.
- `.tropo/system/vault-steward.template.md` — the 9-function verifier reads/writes resolve under `vault/`; no `system/updates/` path assumptions; regression checks run against the single `vault/` tree.

(These are *re-validations against the new boundary*, not rewrites of the migration logic.)

### 7. THE FLOOR TEST — the gate's acceptance proof  *(NEW)*

A clean-update test that *proves* the property. Talos mints the UID at build-time; it lands as a `tropo-`-namespaced playbook under `vault/playbooks/`.

The test:
1. **Seed** a throwaway vault with user content named `<slug>-<uid>` (and bare `<uid>.md`) across user areas — record each file's mtime and content hash.
2. **Apply** an update package whose operations replace `tropo-*` OS components (a real `replace` op set against shipped components).
3. **Assert ZERO user-file churn** — every seeded user file's mtime AND content hash is unchanged.
4. **Assert all OS components updated** — every targeted `tropo-*` component is at the new version.
5. The test **FAILS if a single user file is touched.** A gate that cannot fail when it should is not a gate (the v2-floor program's own discipline, §Gate 4 framing).

This is the artifact that lets Mike walk acceptance-criterion #9 and see the property hold with his own eyes.

### 8. Explicitly OUT of scope — deferred to v3  *(named, not built)*

Per the v2-floor program §Gate 2 and Update Spec v1.1 §14.6, these are **real, named, and deferred** — not forgotten, not pretended-solved:
- **Auto-rollback** of a partially applied update (Spec v1.1 §14.5; the most costly deferral — reconsider first in v3).
- **Migration signing / authorship verification** — a supply-chain surface only once third-party updates exist.
- **Third-party update namespace** (e.g. `<author-id>-update-*`) — namespace-collision risk deferred until a marketplace ships.
- **Batch / sequential apply** of multiple pending updates — v1.1 handles one at a time; the chain-walk is deferred.
- **Hosted telemetry / feedback loop** — verification reports stay local; an opt-in submit endpoint is a separate spec with explicit consent.

If any of these appear in the build, the cycle has overshot the floor.

---

## How to validate / how to test

*(Carried per the locked rule from Update Spec v1.1 — every spec states how its claims would be tested.)*

1. **Namespace predicate is deterministic** — feed the apply engine a mixed file set (`tropo-foo.md` + `bar-1a2b3c4d.md` + `1a2b3c4d.md`); assert it marks only the `tropo-*` file for replace and leaves the rest untouched. No content read required for the decision.
2. **Playbook reconciliation is complete** — `grep` the canonical `vault/playbooks/71f186cf.md` for `system/updates/` and for the SHA-drift block; both return zero. The namespace-predicate Rule is present and cites `ca6e5824`.
3. **Update API contract** — curl the three response shapes (up-to-date, available, migration_required) and assert JSON shape; curl a malformed version and assert graceful (non-5xx, well-formed); simulate offline and assert the agent skips with no error state.
4. **Incompatibility halt** — point a below-`minimum_supported` vault at an update; assert the agent delivers the `message` verbatim and halts before op 1; assert `.tropo/version.md` unchanged.
5. **State machine re-home** — assert pending/applied/failed + history resolve under `vault/`; assert no code path reads or writes `system/updates/`.
6. **v1.1 mechanisms intact** — re-run the v1.1 test battery against the reconciled playbook: backward-compat, idempotency, dry-run accuracy, defensive skip, version-gap guidance — all still pass.
7. **Reference migrations + steward** — run both migrations and the steward against a current single-vault studio; assert scopes resolve, no `tropo-*`/`.tropo/` write by a migration, steward regression passes.
8. **THE FLOOR TEST** (acceptance-criterion #9) — the seed → apply → assert-zero-churn run is the gate proof.

**What passing proves:** the OS updates and user work survives, by construction (predicate) and by demonstration (floor test). **What it does NOT prove:** behavior under the deferred v3 dimensions (rollback, signing, third-party namespace, batch apply, telemetry) — those are named OUT and untested here by design.

## Lane + process

- **Lane:** Argus specs and verifies; **Talos builds**, inside a **real dev-pipeline activation** (no ad-hoc dispatch). The dev-pipeline engine fires coupled doc + test activations off this dev-spec; the cycle cannot close until they close clean (dev-spec.capsule Rule 3, three-pipeline coupling).
- **Sequence:** This gate hard-depends on the **One Home formal close (v1.76)** — it needs the settled `tropo-*` / `<slug>-<uid>` namespace boundary to stand on. Per the v2-floor program §Sequence, Gate 2 is Track B: start after the v1.76 close.
- **Cut:** **v1.78.0**, its own release, sequenced after the v1.76 One Home close. *Sequence-not-fixed:* the number is a label, not the ordering (v2/v3 reframe); Vela reconciles release numbers to actual cut-order if v1.75 (drift) and v1.76 (One Home) invert. The proposal is "the next sensible semver after v1.76," i.e. v1.78.0.
- **Mike signs** the produce gate of the v1.78.0 cut (Gate 5 — the irreducible human Pipeline-Key step).
